assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full; driver_capability: ready

This is a RE-ASSESSMENT. The previous verdict was `daemon=bug`, anchored to `parseToolCalls` dropping `function.arguments` so that `SessionMetrics.Tasks` was never populated. That gap is CLOSED in this worktree by commit 4b65f639 (`fix(hermes): surface the todo tool's task list; share the task fold with opencode`), and the daemon pillar is re-judged below against the CURRENT code, which I re-read in full.

## Reasoning

### agent_supports: yes (unchanged)

Hermes Agent's single-session task-list primitive is the **`todo`** tool (Claude Code uses TaskCreate/TaskUpdate; OpenCode `todowrite`; gemini-cli `write_todos`; codex `update_plan`). The shipped source is authoritative: `tools/todo_tool.py` declares `TODO_SCHEMA = {"name": "todo", ...}` with a `todos` array whose items are `{id: string, content: string, status: string}` and `VALID_STATUSES = {"pending", "in_progress", "completed", "cancelled"}`, and registers it with `registry.register(name="todo", toolset="todo", ...)`. The module docstring states the semantics the scenario needs: "Provides an in-memory task list the agent uses to decompose complex tasks, track progress", "Single `todo` tool: provide `todos` param to write, omit to read", "Every call returns the full current list". `merge=false` (the default) is a FULL-LIST REPLACE — structurally identical to opencode's `todowrite` — and `merge=true` updates existing items by id. The schema description pins the walk the scenario asserts: "Only ONE item in_progress at a time. Mark items completed immediately when done."

The tool runs inside the agent's own turn loop (an in-memory `TodoStore` on the AIAgent instance, one per session) — it spawns no child session and writes no `parent_session_id`, so `SubagentCount` stays 0. Hermes' subagent primitive is a different tool (`delegate_task`, `tools/delegate_tool.py`), which the recipe explicitly forbids.

It is enabled by default on the surfaces this cell records: `toolsets.py:54` lists `"todo"` under "# Planning & memory" in the default CLI/messaging tool set, and again in the `coding` (`toolsets.py:362`) and `hermes-acp` (`toolsets.py:394`) toolsets. `check_todo_requirements()` returns `True` unconditionally ("Todo tool has no external requirements -- always available"), so there is no provider or model gate of the kind that constrains gemini-cli's `write_todos`.

### daemon_capability: full (was `bug`; re-judged on the fixed code)

The scenario's load-bearing observable is "three task items appear in the session API `tasks` field with matching subjects, each progressing pending → in_progress → completed, while SubagentCount stays 0 and state follows ready → working → ready". Every clause of that is produced by the adapter as it stands today.

**The todo payload now survives parse.** `parser.go`'s `toolCall` struct (lines 136–143) carries `Function.Arguments`, `decodeToolCalls` (147–157) unmarshals the `messages.tool_calls` column into it once, and `ParseLine` (103–107) both reports the calls as `ToolUses` AND mines them: `p.todos.Reconcile(todosFromCalls(calls), ev)`. `todosFromCalls` (189–209) decodes the double-encoded `arguments` JSON string into `{todos: [{content, status}]}` and hands each item over as a `tailer.Todo{Key: content, Status: status}` — hermes' exact schema per `todo_tool.py`. `tailer.TodoReconciler.Reconcile` (`core/pkg/tailer/todo_reconciler.go:37-75`) turns each whole-list snapshot into the minimal Create/Update delta sequence plus a `TaskSnapshot`. The reconciler is a field on `Parser`, and `foldMessages` builds a fresh `&Parser{}` per poll and replays every row in `timestamp ASC, id ASC` order (`metrics.go:195-229`), so the synthetic ids are rebuilt deterministically on every `ComputeMetrics` call rather than drifting with poll timing.

**The fold now reaches the API field.** `messageFold` carries `tasks []session.Task` + `taskByID` (`metrics.go:180-190`), `apply` folds each event through the shared `tailer.ApplyTaskDeltas` / `tailer.ReconcileTaskSnapshot` (`metrics.go:245-248`), and `querySessionMetrics` assigns `metrics.Tasks = fold.tasks` (`metrics.go:141`). Those two helpers are the rules hoisted out of opencode into `core/pkg/tailer/task_fold.go` by the same commit — Create starts a task at pending, Update advances it, and the whole-list snapshot is authoritative for BOTH pruning vanished items and the status reversions the delta path deliberately skips. opencode now calls the same functions, so the two ProcessOwnedStore adapters cannot drift.

Applied to the recipe's traffic: the first `todo` call (three items, all `pending`) emits three Creates → `Tasks` = three `session.Task` rows with `Subject` = the three contents at `pending`; each subsequent call's snapshot moves exactly one item to `in_progress` then `completed`, which the Update deltas apply and the snapshot re-asserts. `cancelled` — hermes' fourth status, which no other adapter has — passes through verbatim as a status string; it is not exercised by this recipe.

**Confirmed by tests, seen red first.** `TestParseLine_TodoToolCallProducesTaskDeltas` and `TestParseLine_TodoToolCallSecondSnapshotIsDeltaOnly` (`parser_test.go:149,185`) and `TestComputeMetrics_TodoToolCallsPopulateTasks` (`metrics_test.go:366`, which drives the real SQLite store end-to-end) are recorded in 4b65f639's message as having failed before the fix (`len(Tasks) = 0, want 3`); `TestParseLine_TodoExtractionIsNarrowAndSafe` (`parser_test.go:208`) is a LOCK pinning that non-todo calls are never mined and malformed arguments degrade to zero deltas. All green here: `go test ./core/adapters/inbound/agents/hermes/... ./core/pkg/tailer/... ./core/adapters/inbound/agents/opencode/... -count=1` → 3/3 ok (opencode included, since its fold was rehosted).

**The rest of the arc was already observable and is untouched.** `finish_reason` is an explicit turn boundary (`parser.go:108-110` maps `assistant`/`stop` to `turn_done`; the watcher's `turnIsDone` marks the activity event Terminal), so ready → working → ready settles without an idle heuristic, and the intervening `todo` calls hold the session in `working` via the open-tool-call set — note `ParseLine` deliberately still reports the todo call as a `ToolUse`, so mining it does not leave a tool open that never closes. No child session is created, so `SubagentCount` stays 0.

The one thing the daemon still does NOT produce for hermes is a `task_delta` LIFECYCLE EVENT in `events.jsonl`. That is not this cell's bug and not a hermes property: `SessionMetrics.AppliedTaskDeltas` — the slice `SessionDetector.recordTaskDeltas` (`session_detector_activity.go:746-750`) iterates — is written in exactly two places, both inside the tailer's scan loop (`core/pkg/tailer/tailer.go:977,1024`; verified by `grep -rn AppliedTaskDeltas --include=*.go core/`), and a `ProcessOwnedStore` adapter bypasses the tailer by construction. opencode is in the identical position and its task-list cell is assessed `daemon=full` at confidence 0.9. Per the skill's "caveats over downgrades" rule this is a caveat (tracked as #662), not a `bug`: the spec-required observable — the session API `tasks` field — IS produced. The consequence for this cell is a spec one, recorded below.

### driver_capability: ready (unchanged)

The recipe needs `send`, `wait_turn` and `sleep`. All three are genuinely ported in `replaydata/agents/hermes/driver-interactive.sh`: `DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash sleep wait_turn"` (line 113), `send_text` types the literal text then Enter after a 0.4s beat, and `wait_turn` (SEAM 2) polls the store for `COUNT(*) FROM messages WHERE session_id=... AND role='assistant' AND finish_reason='stop'` exceeding `EXPECTED_TURNS_SEEN` — a real signal poll on Hermes' explicit turn marker, not an idle guess. Launch is `hermes chat` under tmux with `wait_for_prompt` polling for the ready banner. No stubbed arm (`interrupt`, `keys`, `reset_session`, `restart`, `resume`, `sigkill`, `exit_clean`, `start_session`, `session`) is required by this recipe.

Interactive rather than headless deliberately: Hermes' one-shot `-z` mode exits at turn completion, so the process would not outlive the daemon's observation window and the settle phase would validate as missing.

## Spec note — why there is no `task_tracked` phase

The previous spec carried a `{"phase":"task_tracked","kind":"task_delta"}` line under `known_failing`. It is dropped, for two reasons that both point the same way. First, that phase can never pass for a ProcessOwnedStore adapter regardless of how correct the task fold is (see the `AppliedTaskDeltas` finding above), so keeping it would pin the cell at `record-known-failing` and misreport a fixed daemon as broken. Second, no sibling task-list spec asserts it: claudecode, opencode, kiro-cli and mistral-vibe — all `daemon=full`, all recorded/observed — assert the lifecycle arc only, and the verify engine (`tools/onboarding-factory/internal/validate/expected.go`) can match only `state_transition` states and event `kind`s from `events.jsonl`; it has no way to read a session's `tasks` payload at all. The tasks observable therefore lives where every other cell puts it: the recipe's `verify` checklist, against the store and the session API.

## Recording notes

Hermes is a presession adapter for spec-anchoring purposes: it declares a `ProcessMatcher` (`agent.go:32-36`), so `processlifecycle`'s scanner mints a transient `proc-<PID>` row at launch, while the real `sessions` row — and therefore the real session id, shaped `YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_<hex6>` — is INSERTed only on the first user message, ~2s later (`adapter.go` package doc). The spec therefore models the birth as two phases and anchors every later phase to the real session, per the presession template.
caveats: PROVISIONAL ON EMISSION (the reason confidence is 0.8, not 0.9): the sample store still carries no `todo` call (`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages WHERE tool_calls LIKE '%"todo"%'` → 0 over 11 sessions / 117 message rows), so the persisted argument shape the parser now decodes is taken from hermes' own tools/todo_tool.py rather than read off a live row. What IS confirmed from the live store is the envelope the fix depends on: every `tool_calls` row persists `function.arguments` verbatim as a double-encoded JSON string (e.g. terminal's `"{\"command\":\"ls ...\"}"`). `record` promotes this from provisional to settled.

events.jsonl carries NO task payload for hermes, so the tasks observable is not machine-asserted by a spec phase — it is checked by the recipe's `verify` checklist. SessionMetrics.AppliedTaskDeltas (what SessionDetector.recordTaskDeltas turns into task_delta lifecycle events) is written only inside the tailer scan loop (tailer.go:977,1024), and a ProcessOwnedStore adapter bypasses the tailer; opencode — assessed daemon=full — is in the identical position. Tracked as #662; closing it would let a future spec add the phase for both adapters at once.

Todos are keyed by `content`, not by hermes' stable per-todo `id`, because tailer.Todo.Key doubles as TaskDelta.Subject and an agent-chosen id like "t2" is not something to show a user. Two todos with identical content collapse into one tracked task — the documented trade-off every TodoReconciler caller makes. The recipe's three subjects are deliberately distinct, so this cannot bite this recording; an agent that reworded a todo mid-run would instead create a second task rather than rename the first.

`cancelled` is a hermes-only fourth status (VALID_STATUSES in todo_tool.py). It passes through the fold verbatim as a status string and is NOT exercised by this recipe, so this cell says nothing about how it renders downstream.

`model` and `cost` are deliberately left unpinned in observations. The recording home's model is a human choice, and irrlicht prices hermes via its own alias table rather than the store's `estimated_cost_usd` (which the local store reports as 0.0 under subscription billing): the locally configured `gpt-5.6-luna` has no entry in core/pkg/capacity/aliases.go, and EstimateCostUSD returns 0 for an unpriced model (core/pkg/capacity/capacity.go:159-162), so a `cost_nonzero` assertion would fail for reasons unrelated to this scenario. `tokens_nonzero` is safe — the sessions row carries input/output token aggregates (observed 16269/5 on a live row).

`hermes chat` records `source='cli'`, and Hermes populates `sessions.cwd` only from its TUI gateway, so the session's project binding comes from the live-process CWD fallback (watcher.go:115-124 / metrics.go:119-122), which returns "" when zero or more than one hermes session process is alive. A concurrent hermes session during recording would leave the cell's cwd unbound; not asserted by this spec, but it affects project-dir attribution.

CONFIRMED by recording 2026-08-02-23-43-35_irrlichd-0.5.9+2804b23 (2026-08-02): 5/5 spec phases pass AND the cell's real claim — commit 4b65f639's todo-tool task lift — is demonstrated. The live store shape matches what parser.go was written against WITHOUT having been read from a live store first: assistant tool_calls rows carry [{"type":"function","function":{"name":"todo","arguments":"{\"todos\":[{\"id\":...,\"content\":...,\"status\":...}]}"}}] — arguments a JSON *string*, todos a whole-list snapshot, statuses pending|in_progress|completed. The generated golden's summary.tasks is [{read README, completed}, {summarize README, completed}, {reply done, completed}], i.e. decodeToolCalls -> todosFromCalls -> TodoReconciler -> ApplyTaskDeltas/ReconcileTaskSnapshot -> metrics.Tasks works end to end on real data. 6 todo calls, 16 store rows, 30 daemon events.

LATENT GAP found while confirming the shape (not a defect of this recording, and NOT exercised by it): hermes' todo tool takes a second parameter `merge` (todo_tool.py:59,206 — merge=false replaces the whole list, merge=true updates existing items BY ID and adds new ones). The live calls here carried merge absent on the first call and merge:false on all five later ones, so every call really was a whole-list snapshot. todosFromCalls (parser.go:223-242) ignores `merge` entirely and hands every call's todos to TodoReconciler as a full snapshot — so a merge:true call carrying only the changed item would reconcile as 'the list is now one item' and silently drop the rest. Unverified whether any hermes prompt path actually elicits merge:true; the fix is correct for every shape observed so far.

observations: tokens_nonzero STRIPPED (seen red on this recording: `✗ tokens: want >0 got 0`, all state phases green) and `model` pinned in its place — same unsatisfiability, same reason as the committed 2-1 / 1-1 / 2-13 cells. The assessment note above claiming 'tokens_nonzero is safe - the sessions row carries input/output aggregates' is wrong about the path: the sessions aggregate reaches irrlicht only through ComputeMetrics, which the offline replay tool never runs.

sources.note: TODO_SCHEMA name="todo", items {id, content, status}, VALID_STATUSES pending|in_progress|completed|cancelled, merge=false is a full-list replace, registry.register(name="todo", toolset="todo"), check_todo_requirements() always True. This is the schema todosFromCalls decodes.
"todo" is in the default CLI tool list ("# Planning & memory"), its own `todo` toolset, and the `coding` + `hermes-acp` toolsets — enabled by default on the surfaces this cell records.

THE FIX (commit 4b65f639), re-read for this assessment: toolCall now carries Function.Arguments; decodeToolCalls unmarshals the column once; ParseLine reports the calls as ToolUses AND calls p.todos.Reconcile(todosFromCalls(calls), ev); todosFromCalls decodes the double-encoded arguments into {todos:[{content,status}]} keyed by content. Supersedes the previous assessment's citation of parseToolCalls dropping function.arguments.

messageFold now carries tasks/taskByID; apply() folds every event through tailer.ApplyTaskDeltas + tailer.ReconcileTaskSnapshot; querySessionMetrics assigns metrics.Tasks = fold.tasks. foldMessages builds a fresh &Parser{} per poll and replays rows ORDER BY timestamp ASC, id ASC, so the reconciler's synthetic ids are deterministic.

The shared whole-list-snapshot machinery hermes now uses: Reconcile emits Create (starts at pending) + Update deltas and a TaskSnapshot; ApplyTaskDeltas/ReconcileTaskSnapshot fold them into []session.Task, the snapshot being authoritative for pruning and for reversions. Hoisted out of opencode by 4b65f639 so the two ProcessOwnedStore adapters share one implementation.

TestParseLine_TodoToolCallProducesTaskDeltas / _SecondSnapshotIsDeltaOnly / TestComputeMetrics_TodoToolCallsPopulateTasks (drives the real SQLite store, asserts three Tasks with the right subjects and statuses) — recorded as seen red pre-fix in 4b65f639's message. TestParseLine_TodoExtractionIsNarrowAndSafe is a LOCK (non-todo calls are never mined; malformed arguments yield no deltas). Re-run for this assessment: go test ./core/adapters/inbound/agents/hermes/... ./core/pkg/tailer/... ./core/adapters/inbound/agents/opencode/... -count=1 → all ok.

Anchors the events.jsonl caveat: AppliedTaskDeltas (which recordTaskDeltas turns into task_delta lifecycle events) is assigned ONLY in the tailer scan loop — `grep -rn AppliedTaskDeltas --include=*.go core/` finds no other writer — so no ProcessOwnedStore adapter (hermes, opencode) records task_delta events. #662.

The matrix precedent this verdict is aligned to: opencode's task-list cell is agent=yes/daemon=full/driver=ready at confidence 0.9 on the same whole-list-replace shape, same ProcessOwnedStore transport, same absence of task_delta events — and its spec asserts the lifecycle arc only (as do claudecode's, kiro-cli's and mistral-vibe's).

The verify engine matches a phase only by expected_state (a state_transition's new_state) or by event kind, over the recordedEvent subset {ts, kind, session_id, new_state}. There is no mechanism to assert a session's tasks payload — which is why the tasks observable lives in the recipe's verify checklist.

Live store, 11 sessions / 117 message rows. `SELECT tool_calls FROM messages WHERE tool_calls IS NOT NULL LIMIT 1` shows function.arguments persisted verbatim as a double-encoded JSON string; `SELECT COUNT(*) ... LIKE '%"todo"%'` → 0 (still no todo call recorded — the basis of the provisional caveat).

DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash sleep wait_turn"; send_text, wait_turn (store poll on finish_reason='stop') and the launch/wait_for_prompt seams are ported — the stubbed arms this recipe never reaches are interrupt/keys/reset_session/restart/resume/sigkill/exit_clean/start_session/session.

ProcessMatcher declared (so processlifecycle mints a transient proc-<PID> presession), while the real sessions row is INSERTed ~2s after launch on the first user message — the presession/real-session split the spec's two-phase birth is anchored to.

recipe.prompt: Use your todo tool to create exactly three todo items, in this order: 'read README', 'summarize README', 'reply done'. Then work them one at a time: for each item call todo again to set that item's status to in_progress, then call todo again to set it to completed, before moving on to the next one. Keep everything in this one session - do NOT use delegate_task or spawn any subagent. When all three items are completed, reply with exactly the word: done
verify: state.db messages contains assistant rows whose tool_calls carry function.name='todo' with a todos[] snapshot walking the three items 'read README' / 'summarize README' / 'reply done' from pending through in_progress to completed

the session API tasks field lists exactly those three items as subjects, all ending completed (this is the load-bearing observable; events.jsonl carries no task_delta for a ProcessOwnedStore adapter, so check it on the session payload, not the event stream)
no delegate_task call and no child session row (parent_session_id stays NULL); SubagentCount stays 0
state follows ready -> working -> ready; final session state is ready
